Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is 9to5Mac's weekly column dedicated to highlighting the latest apps from the indie app scene. If you're a developer and want to pitch your app, feel free to reach out to us.

Farwave designs a music player in an interesting new way, placing them on a globe. You can explore the world, find radio stations from around the globe, and enjoy beautiful 3D visual effects. Podcasts and music you want to listen to can also be explored within the app using their own unique visual effects.

Main Features

Farwave lets you listen to every radio station in the world. You can spin the globe, find a region, and tap on a station. If you want to listen to something random, there's also a "Take Me Anywhere" button. The app also provides listening history, making it easy to revisit those stations later.

In addition to radio stations, Farwave also offers podcasts and music—each with its own independent planet display. You can search for podcasts or add their RSS feeds, and the app also supports playlists, speed adjustment, and offline downloads.

For music, it doesn't support Apple Music, but you can import your music files from your computer or the Files app. Each artist has their own signal, and music is stored on the device for offline playback.

Download the App

Farwave is available for free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad running iOS 18 or later. For the full experience, including podcasts, music import, and more, you can subscribe to FarWave Pro for $2.99 per month or $14.99 per year.
